commitResults.messageTitle: Add regression tests for hyphens and apostrophes in ride names
Address review comments on ride-name tests and manual test steps
Allow hyphens and apostrophes in cyclist names
commitResults.messageBody:
Name validation rejects Tan Wei-Ling and John O'Connor, preventing
organisers from recording these cyclists with their correct spelling.

Allow internal hyphens and straight apostrophes while preserving the
existing Unicode name rules. Continue to reject leading, trailing,
consecutive and space-adjacent punctuation. Apply the same rules to
cyclist edits and ride names through the shared Name validator.

Add regression coverage for both reported commands, name searches,
editing, JSON readback and rejection without saved-data changes.
Update the Developer Guide and testing guidance with the accepted
name formats and manual regression scenarios.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain name validation regression test cases
commitResults.messageBody:
Name validation regression tests cover several Unicode and punctuation
cases without explaining all case groups and setup choices.

Add comments explaining valid and invalid name groups, Unicode edge
cases, search checks, persistence checks and duplicate avoidance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match parts of hyphenated and apostrophised words
commitResults.messageBody:
The find and ridefind commands treat a hyphenated or apostrophised
word as one indivisible word. Since names may now contain internal
hyphens and apostrophes, ridefind n/Wei-Ling does not find Wei-Ling's
Ride, and find n/Ling does not find Tan Wei-Ling.

Treat whitespace, hyphens and apostrophes as word separators in the
shared StringUtil matcher, for both the stored value and the search
criterion. Matching stays case-insensitive, whole-word and ordered, so
fragments such as Lin and WeiLing still do not match. A criterion
containing no word, such as a lone hyphen, now matches nothing instead
of matching every value.

Add unit and integration tests, and update the User Guide, Developer
Guide, testing notes and manual test scenarios.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow slower JavaFX start-up in UI tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The macos-15-intel CI job fails intermittently in the Gradle test
step. It failed on a test-only commit of an earlier pull request and
passed on the next commit without any relevant change. The Intel
hosted VM is slow to start JavaFX, while the UI test helpers allow
only 5 seconds for the toolkit to start and for each task on the
JavaFX thread, and 20 seconds for a child JVM to exit.

Raise the JavaFxToolkit timeout to 30 seconds and the child JVM wait
to 60 seconds. The timeouts only bound how long a test waits, so
passing tests are not slowed down.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore leading zeros in phone numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
Cyclique compares phone numbers as exact text, so the same number
written with leading zeros is accepted as a different cyclist's
number: +065 91234561 and +65 091234561 duplicate +65 91234561, and
+0 000 is saved as a valid number. The uniqueness rule can be bypassed
by accident, and edit, delete and roster commands may then target the
wrong record.

Accept leading zeros in the country code and the number, but require
a non-zero digit in each part and at least 3 digits in the number
after its leading zeros. Remove the leading zeros when constructing a
Phone, so equality, duplicate detection, command targets, find and
ride rosters all treat such numbers as the same number. Extend the
invalid phone message to explain the rule.

Add unit and integration tests, change an edit test that used the now
invalid +65 00000000, and update the User Guide, Developer Guide,
testing notes and manual test scenarios.

Closes #239

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Strip leading zeros from country code only
commitResults.messageBody:
The previous change also removed leading zeros from the main phone
number. Those zeros can be significant, so +39 0612345678 was stored
as +39 612345678, a different number. It also made some saved numbers,
such as +65 00000000, invalid.

Limit the removal to the country code, which must still contain a
non-zero digit. The number is validated and stored as typed, so
+065 91234561 still duplicates +65 91234561 but +65 091234561 does not
duplicate +65 91234561. Shorten the invalid phone message to match.

Update the unit and integration tests, restore the unknown phone used
by EditCommandTest, and update the User Guide (including which older
data files no longer load and how to correct them), Developer Guide,
testing notes and manual test scenarios.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document location searches and the "-" criterion
commitResults.messageBody:
The hyphenated and apostrophised name regression only checked name
searches, so it did not support the claim that find and ridefind match
parts of hyphenated locations. Searching with a cyclist whose location
is "any" would also pass regardless, as "any" matches every search.

Add steps that create a cyclist and a ride at Pasir-Ris Park and check
find l/Ris, find l/Pasir-Ris and ridefind l/Ris list them while the
fragment Ri does not. Add the "-" criterion checks.

Replace the statement that a criterion with no word "matches nothing".
find n/- and ridefind n/- fail name validation, ridefind l/- lists no
rides and find l/- lists only cyclists whose location is "any". Update
the testing notes and release notes to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix wording of the any-location search note
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide said a cyclist whose location is any matches every
location criterion except the literal any. That is wrong: such a
cyclist also matches find l/any. Remove the exception.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore the ride numeric values note
commitResults.messageBody:
The rideadd command has no phone number, so the previous edit to its
leading zeroes note, which referred to country codes, did not belong in
this change. Restore the original line, which is about numeric values.
